paper_id: Ubiquitous memory augmentation via mobile multimodal embedding system
title: Ubiquitous memory augmentation via mobile multimodal embedding system
motivation: Mobile devices generate multimodal data but lack efficient retrieval; MEM inference is too slow and energy-intensive for on-device deployment
problem_framing: On-device multimodal embedding as memory palace service with resource-constrained execution requiring trade-offs between throughput, accuracy, and energy
key_insight: Offload full embedding cost to infrequent query phase via coarse-grained early-exit embeddings, mirroring brain's selective memory retention
method_signature: Early-exit multimodal embedding with data-aware pre-exit prediction, progressive LoRA healing, and speculative fine-grained retrieval
evaluation_criteria: Throughput improvement, retrieval accuracy relative to full model, energy reduction, memory footprint on mobile devices
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Reminisce has slightly higher peak memory than naive layer-wise baseline due to batching parallelism overhead, though still within practical range
evidence_for_taste: early exit aligns with our design principles
little to no benefit during inference
thinking_moves: 把完整的embedding计算卸载到查询阶段
从人脑记忆机制获得设计启发
承认早退出方法的并行度缺陷并提出预判策略
用progressive方式解决LoRA参数共享与精度损失的矛盾
